name: EvenHub Edu
description: A school-management platform with an AI assistant for parents, teachers, and administrators. Connects school documents, events, menus, and lunch orders in one portal.
details: Led a four-person Humber capstone for an external sponsor, delivered May–August 2026. Expanded a working sponsor prototype into a platform used by real people.

Implemented document extraction, chunking, embedding retrieval, semantic reranking, role-aware context, and streamed answers. Read-only Gmail integration and tools connect the assistant to school workflows.

name: BakeOps
description: An AI command center for bakery operations. Routes equipment, supply-chain, and recipe scenarios to specialist agents and brings their recommendations into a live dashboard.
details: Built with Nanditha for the TMLS × FGF Brands Agentic Hackathon; second place in 2026.
An orchestrator selects three specialists, runs selected work in parallel, then synthesizes the results. Includes SSE updates, label analysis, Open Food Facts, and Telegram alerts.
Factory scenarios and dashboard telemetry are simulated; displayed savings are demonstration estimates.

name: SENTINEL
description: A commerce assistant that turns requests and photos into evidence-backed product shortlists and live merchant quotes. A separate sandbox flow demonstrates checkout with explicit approval.
details: Track 1 winner at Agnic.AI Agentic Commerce Pioneers 2026.
Supports product requests, broken-part inspection, and reference-photo bills of materials. Server-side checks verify merchants, quotes, consent, and provider order status.
Real-money purchasing is disabled. Checkout demonstrations use the payment provider’s sandbox; scheduling is runtime-only.

name: Compass
description: A Slack copilot for developer questions about microservices. Retrieves from OpenAPI specifications and documentation, cites its sources, and traces service dependencies.
details: Combines dense retrieval with BM25, reciprocal-rank fusion, and reranking. Keeps API operations intact and uses dependency metadata for impact questions.
Demonstrated against 12 synthetic payment-domain services. Conversation memory is in-process, and the current interface supports direct messages.

name: AutoApply
description: A job-discovery pipeline that collects listings, removes duplicates, applies practical filters, and ranks relevant opportunities with short AI explanations.
details: Integrates Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby listings. Applies cheap filters before model scoring, isolates adapter failures, and writes ranked results in batches.
Working local pipeline with a console digest. It discovers and ranks jobs; it does not submit applications. Email delivery and scheduled cloud execution are not completed.

name: MedSafe
description: A medication-interaction explorer that combines a drug knowledge graph with a web interface to help users inspect relationships between medications.
details: Built with React, Neo4j Aura, Neon PostgreSQL, Prisma, and GraphQL Yoga. Includes authentication and AI integrations for explanations and image-based input.
Academic software demonstration using interaction data. It is not clinically validated and should not be used to make treatment decisions.

name: FactoryVision
description: An image-quality inspection backend that connects a C# API to a Python vision service. Validates uploads, analyses visual quality, and stores inspection history.
details: ASP.NET Core uses dependency injection and a configurable inference provider; EF Core persists metadata in SQLite. Includes Swagger, structured errors, xUnit, and pytest coverage.
OpenCV measures brightness, contrast, and blur. This is a prototype heuristic, not a trained manufacturing-defect detector or a live factory integration.

name: ContextOS
description: A memory-management layer for long-running LLM conversations. Keeps recent turns in hot memory, compresses older turns into summaries, and archives the original text.
details: Tracks token usage and session cost, compresses older messages with Haiku, and displays memory state in a Streamlit dashboard.
The completed core uses a file-based state exchange. Semantic cold-memory retrieval, checkpoint restoration, and RAG features are roadmap items.

name: Speech Emotion Recognition
description: An audio classifier for eight emotions. Compares an ANN, CNN, and CNN–Transformer, then averages their predictions in an ensemble with a Streamlit demo.
details: Uses 4,240 RAVDESS and TESS speech clips, MFCC features, and Mel-spectrograms. A four-person academic submission with CNN implementation and project coordination among Tarun’s contributions.
The project report records 92.3% ensemble accuracy on an 848-clip held-out test set. This is a clip-level split on acted speech; speaker-disjoint evaluation is not established.

name: Jetson / Edge AI
description: An object-detection pipeline exploring accelerated inference on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, bringing computer-vision workloads onto an edge device.
details: Uses model export and TensorRT FP16 optimisation, with Flask for a lightweight application interface.
Focuses on deployment and inference acceleration. Hardware benchmark conditions are not documented here, so no throughput or latency claim is presented.

name: SubGenie
description: A subscription manager that tracks recurring costs and usage, calculates cost per use, and offers AI suggestions for cutting underused services or finding alternatives.
details: Includes authenticated subscription management, usage logs, analytics, and an AI advisor. A natural-language Telegram bot supports everyday tracking and reminders.
MongoDB and Mongoose store user-scoped data; JWT and bcrypt support authentication. The interface uses server-rendered EJS, Tailwind, and Chart.js.

name: FATHOM
description: An evidence-first browser automation tool for researching Ontario auto-insurance journeys. Records observations and blocked steps through a deterministic action-policy gate.
details: Second prize at the MyChoice Ontario All-Quote Agent Challenge 2026. Captures timestamped, redacted evidence and distinguishes refusals from unresolved attempts.
No real insurer returned a price under the hypothetical profile in this build. Comparable price examples come from a labelled local sandbox; the tool does not purchase policies.

name: AEOscope
description: A website auditor for SEO and answer-engine readiness. Checks page structure, schema, and content clarity, then uses Claude to identify information gaps in a brand’s website.
details: Produces SEO and AEO scores, prioritised recommendations, and Markdown or JSON reports. A no-AI mode runs the rule-based checks without an API key.
The AI perception report is a simulation based on supplied website content; it does not measure rankings or directly query every search engine.

name: ORCA AI
description: A prompt-to-web-app workflow that generates code, writes project files, pushes to GitHub, deploys through Railway, and validates the result with a browser.
details: Uses multiple AI providers with ordered fallback, an in-process event queue, and a dashboard for build stages and logs.
A failed build can trigger one AI repair attempt. Tool adapters coordinate browser, GitHub, shell, and deployment work; this does not imply a production-grade recovery system.

name: PerkPal
description: A community-focused deals platform for discovering relevant offers by audience and category, with registration, login, personalised offer pages, and a wishlist interface.
details: Static frontend pages organise offers for students, seniors, and other communities. The personalised flow connects to a separate local backend API.
Built as a web-development project. The public frontend repository is not a complete hosted full-stack service.

name: Alberta AI Gateway
description: An AI-assisted tourism and travel platform for Alberta. Combines trip planning, conversational help, speech features, local events and weather, and interactive 3D content.
details: Second place at the Brainstem Alliance Hackathon 2025; built and led during a three-day sprint.
React frontend and Express API integrate OpenAI, Gemini, Ticketmaster, and OpenWeather. JWT authentication and MongoDB support accounts and saved itineraries.

name: Sentiment Analysis / NLP Research
description: A product-review sentiment-classification study using Logistic Regression and Naive Bayes, published as “Public Relationships using NLP and Machine Learning.”
details: Published in IJCRT, volume 12, issue 5, May 2024. Tarun is a co-author of the academic paper.
Explores classical machine-learning approaches to review classification. The paper link provides the research context and reported findings.
